source: General Social Survey panels (NORC at the University of Chicago): 2006-08-10, 2008-10-12, 2010-12-14 and 2016/2018-2020, official Stata files from gss.norc.org
target: Probability that a currently married respondent is divorced or separated at the re-interview two years later (prospective; widowhood excluded; a probability over 2 years, not an annual rate)
population: U.S. adults (18+) in households, married at a GSS panel interview in 2006-2018 and re-interviewed two years later; the respondent's own report
weights: NORC panel weights with non-response adjustment (WTPANNR12, WTPANNR123, WTSSNR_2), normalised to mean 1
constant_rate_note: annual-equivalent rate -ln(1 - p)/2 implied by the 2-year probability, for comparison with the rate lenses only

inputs.childs: number of children ever had, 0-8 (8 = eight or more) (CHILDS)
inputs.attend: religious service attendance 0 never ... 8 more than once a week (ATTEND)
inputs.hapmar: 'Taken all together, how would you describe your marriage?' Very happy / Pretty happy / Not too happy (HAPMAR)
inputs.happy: general happiness: Very happy / Pretty happy / Not too happy (HAPPY)
inputs.family_income: family income in constant 2000 dollars (NORC CONINC), banded; multiply 2024 dollars by about 0.55 (CPI-U 172.2/313.7)
inputs.same_religion: Same / Different: RELIG equals SPREL at the detailed code
inputs.divorced_before: ever been divorced or legally separated before (DIVORCE item, asked of the currently married)
inputs.family_at_16: lived with both own parents at 16; if not, whether because of divorce/separation or a death (FAMILY16, FAMDIF16)
inputs.health: self-rated health (HEALTH; split ballot, about two-thirds asked)
inputs.fefam: 'Better for everyone if the man achieves outside the home and the woman takes care of the home and family' (FEFAM; split ballot)
inputs.sexfreq: frequency of sex in the last 12 months (SEXFREQ; self-administered, wave 1 of the 2006-2010 panels only)
inputs.evstray: ever had sex with someone other than the spouse while married (EVSTRAY; self-administered, wave 1 of the 2006-2010 panels only)
inputs.xmarsex: attitude to a married person having sex with someone other than the spouse (XMARSEX; split ballot)

evaluation: StratifiedGroupKFold by respondent, 5 folds x 10 repeats; L1 penalty chosen by inner grouped 4-fold CV within each training fold; weighted log loss, AUC and Brier; 95% CIs from 1000 respondent-cluster bootstrap resamples of the out-of-fold predictions
abstain: anyone not currently married (this lens starts from a married respondent)
any numeric input outside the support
a lifetime or per-year estimate: the target is the 2-year chance only
same-sex couples (too few in the panels to say anything)

models.label: Additive L1 logistic, all inputs (splines for age, children, attendance)

boosted_trees.reason: held-out comparison only; app/engine.js has no logistic gradient-boosting kind

population_reference.note: Survey-weighted quantiles of HELD-OUT predicted dissolution probability (logistic_additive, out-of-fold, averaged over 10 repeats) among married respondents. Cells with fewer than 100 respondents are suppressed. Aggregates only; no person-level values.

models_extended.label: Additive L1 logistic, current inputs + religion detail (9-level attendance, prayer, strength, fundamentalism, denomination, religion raised) + political views and party

heldout.evaluation: C = 0.3 fixed, 5 folds x 5 seeds grouped by respondent; paired respondent-cluster bootstrap (1000)

models_extended.label: Additive L1 logistic, current inputs + all new blocks (family of origin, religion detail, politics, race detail, occupation, wealth)

heldout.evaluation: C = 0.3 fixed, 5 folds x 5 seeds grouped by respondent; paired respondent-cluster bootstrap (1000)

models_extended_note: Held-out comparison of richer inputs (2026-10-20, extended_predictors.py). Not scored by the app until the form asks for the new inputs; a new input left out is scored at its own "Unknown" level (categorical) or the training median (numeric). Blocks whose held-out difference over the current model had a 95% CI above zero: none.

inputs_extended.family_origin: who the respondent lived with at 16 (FAMILY16) and, if not both own parents, why (FAMDIF16): Both parents / Parents divorced or separated / Parent died / Stepfamily (a parent and a step-parent, any reason) / Other (relatives, other reasons; the GSS does not separate never-married single parents)
inputs_extended.attend9: religious service attendance, all nine ATTEND answers (Never ... Every week / More than once a week)
inputs_extended.pray: how often the respondent prays (PRAY), six answers
inputs_extended.religious_strength: strength of religious affiliation (RELITEN): Strong / Somewhat strong / Not very strong / No religion
inputs_extended.fundamentalism: the respondent's religion as fundamentalist / moderate / liberal (NORC's FUND coding of RELIG and DENOM)
inputs_extended.denomination: religion with Protestant denomination families (RELIG, DENOM)
inputs_extended.polviews: political views, 7 points from extremely liberal to extremely conservative (POLVIEWS)
inputs_extended.party: party identification, 7 points plus other party (PARTYID)
inputs_extended.race_detail: race and Hispanic origin from RACECEN1-2 and HISPANIC: White, Black, Hispanic (any race), Asian, American Indian or Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, Multiracial, Other
inputs_extended.sibs: number of brothers and sisters (SIBS), 0-15 (15 = 15 or more)
inputs_extended.parent_education: higher of father's and mother's years of schooling (PAEDUC, MAEDUC), 0-20
inputs_extended.income_at_16: family income at 16 compared with American families in general (INCOM16)
inputs_extended.occupation_group: respondent's current or last occupation (OCC10), Census major group
inputs_extended.home: owns or rents the home (DWELOWN, split ballot)
inputs_extended.wealth_band: household wealth, all assets minus debts (WEALTH; asked in 2006 and 2016-2018 only)
